newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STATE CONCERN BUYS MEIKLES STOCK.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STATE CONCERN BUYS MEIKLES STOCK.

text.p: Zimbabwe's state social security authority, NSSA, has bought more than one million shares of hotel and supermarket group Meikles Africa with one of its officials saying on Friday it intended to invest more in the stock market.
"We have bought a huge chunk of (Meikles) stock and we will continue investing members' money in a prudent way," NSSA investment manager Marshall Nyamakanga told Reuters.
"At the moment we are channelling it into equity rather than the money market because the gains there (in stocks) are higher."

But he refused to be drawn into saying how much and at what price the shares were acquired, saying since the National Social Security Authority was a big player on the market, financial details of the deal would affect its price.
However, Meikles Africa group secretary Bill Lant said: "The transfer papers we have indicate that NSSA has so far bought 1,080,000 shares in Meikles but they might be buying more.'
The group has a total of 156 million shares trading on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange and the London bourse.
Lant and the brokers involved in the deal also declined to say how much NSSA paid for the shares.

NSSA was set up by the government and all employers and employees are compulsorily required to contribute to it. Since it started operating in 1994, it has collected about Z$1.44 billion in contributions.
